title: Van Allen Probe A reentry lesson deposit
summary: Probe A reentered earlier than long-range estimates because stronger solar-cycle drag accelerated decay after the mission had already ended from propellant exhaustion.
body: This event should teach Gauss that apparent spacecraft failure headlines can hide coupled causal chains. The mission end state in 2019 was driven by propellant depletion, attitude constraints, and solar-array pointing limits, while the 2026 reentry timing was driven by stronger-than-expected solar maximum drag. The lesson for near-term causal inference is to keep solar-wind and geomagnetic coupling as the first-order operational drivers, while carrying long-horizon drag and contamination uncertainty explicitly.
lessons: Treat fuel and attitude margin as first-class mission risk drivers.
Carry solar-cycle drag uncertainty in orbital lifetime and reentry forecasts.
Apply confidence penalties to inner-belt measurements vulnerable to proton contamination.
Keep causal weighting on solar-wind and IMF coupling instead of speculative tertiary priors.
